clue.text: Point-to-points in South Africa

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a place found in that country

parts.note: a cape is a point of land jutting into the sea
taken as written
W and N are two compass points, west and north

explanation.surface: A horse-racing fixture of point-to-point races being held in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point-to-points' looks like the steeplechase meetings popular in rural Britain, but it splits into point, to, points.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the legislative capital of the republic, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Hired hands?

parts.note: not farm labourers but people paid to clap their hands at a performance

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's paid band of applauders is employed to clap, so they are hands for hire.

clue.text: Gloomy type from Poland's capital misses it badly

indicators.note: the capital, or leading letter, of the word Poland is wanted
done badly, the letters of the words misses it are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone downcast because a Polish capital-city trip went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poland's capital' suggests Warsaw, but it is only the initial P; 'badly' turns MISSES IT into ESSIMIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A pessimist always expects the worst, the very picture of a gloomy person.

clue.text: Blunder in rank for reservist

indicators.note: the word for the blunder is placed inside the word for rank

parts.note: a tier is a row or rank, as of seats
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A reserve soldier makes a blunder while standing in the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: A terrier is British slang for a member of the Territorial Army, the volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British term for a Territorial Army volunteer, a part-time soldier held in reserve.

clue.text: Writer's sources

definitions.meaning: H. G. ..., the English novelist, read with 's as 'is'
springs or boreholes from which water comes

explanation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells wrote The War of the Worlds; wells are springs where water is drawn, its origins.

clue.text: Doubtless he wasn't a Bohemian poet

definitions.text: Doubtless he wasn't a Bohemian poet

parts.words: Doubtless he wasn't a Bohemian poet
parts.note: the apostle famed for doubting was not without doubt, and the Welsh poet of that surname was Welsh rather than Bohemian

explanation.definitionFit: The apostle who doubted the Resurrection shares a surname with Dylan, the Welsh poet.

clue.text: Courage from tragic priestess over doctrine

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, or above, the second

parts.note: Hero, priestess of Aphrodite, drowned herself after Leander perished swimming to her
an ism is any doctrine or belief system

explanation.surface: Bravery shown by a doomed priestess who stands above dogma.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroism is bravery displayed in the face of danger, a synonym of courage.

clue.text: Country included in formal talks

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the words formal talks

explanation.surface: A nation taking part in official diplomatic negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island republic is a sovereign state.

clue.text: With us, least change in meaning creates uncertainty

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for meaning

parts.note: sense is meaning, as in the sense of a word
taken as written
P, a penny, is the smallest coin of British change

explanation.surface: A tiny alteration in what something means leaves us unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'least change' reads as a minimal alteration, but it is a penny, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious state of not knowing how things will turn out.

clue.text: Longfellow? Not this volume

parts.note: not the American poet but a tall fellow; the opposite is a short person, and also a measure of beer half the usual size

explanation.definitionFit: A small person is informally called by the name of a small beer measure, the reverse of a tall fellow.

clue.text: Eg Victorian laws for sport

definitions.meaning: regulations of a state in Australia such as Victoria
the football code born in Melbourne

explanation.definitionFit: Australian football began in Victoria; its name sounds like the regulations of an Australian state.

clue.text: Aristotelian principles laid down at an early stage

definitions.text: Aristotelian principles laid down at an early stage

parts.words: Aristotelian principles laid down at an early stage
parts.note: rules for drama of time, place and action, set out early in theatrical history for the stage

explanation.definitionFit: Classical dramatic rules derived from Aristotle's Poetics govern time, place and action in a play.

clue.text: Ship's sails etc split a lot

indicators.note: the word for lot is broken open to take the other piece

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
the rig of a vessel is its sails, masts and rigging

explanation.surface: A vessel's canvas is torn badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship.

clue.text: Liberal in diaries wronged Conservative

indicators.note: the letter for Liberal is placed among the rearranged letters
the letters of diaries are put wrong, into a new order

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician's diaries unfairly treated a Tory opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wronged' makes DISRAEI from DIARIES, and 'in' puts L inside. Benjamin Disraeli was a Conservative Prime Minister, rival of the Liberal Gladstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli led the Tory party and served twice as British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Took up strange pose, exhausted

indicators.note: made strange, the letters of pose are shuffled

parts.note: used up, as in a used battery

explanation.surface: Struck an odd attitude and was worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt or embrace it.

clue.text: Female singer married a noble, in short

parts.note: Vis is the short form of viscount, a nobleman

explanation.surface: A woman vocalist who wed a minor aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female singer' suggests a woman vocalist, but the mavis is the song thrush, a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Mavis is an old word for the song thrush, and the bird sings.

clue.text: Stock name for one from Richmond

parts.note: Virginia stock is a flowering garden plant

explanation.surface: A common name for someone from Richmond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' is not standard but the plant; Richmond is the capital of Virginia, not the London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the US state whose capital city is Richmond.

clue.text: Two hours at sea for two hunters, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a half watch of two hours on board ship
a hound used in hunting, and a hunter pocket-watch with a hinged cover

explanation.definitionFit: Ships split a four-hour duty into two-hour spells; a hound and a hunter timepiece together.

clue.text: Ready for gentle stroke to leg?

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a tap is a light blow

explanation.surface: A batsman poised to play a soft shot to the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap, like draught beer, is available and ready whenever needed.

clue.text: Empire's collapse from which a conclusion can be drawn

definitions.text: from which a conclusion can be drawn

indicators.note: the letters of Empire's fall apart and are rebuilt

parts.note: the full letters including the S

explanation.surface: The fall of an empire as a lesson for history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse' rearranges EMPIRES; the S of the possessive is used as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A premise is a proposition in logic that leads to an inference.

clue.text: They play in diamonds or clubs

definitions.meaning: baseball players who throw to the batter on the diamond
golf irons once used for lofted shots

explanation.definitionFit: Baseball throwers work on the diamond; old lofted golf irons were so called.

clue.text: Dangerous place for Pole, in 'a stew

indicators.note: the letter for the pole goes into the stew

parts.note: hotpot is a stew, as in Lancashire hotpot
S, the south pole

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is S, south pole. Lancashire hotpot is a British stew of meat and sliced potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspot is a trouble zone, such as a war zone.

clue.text: Alliance has quite a long way to go

definitions.meaning: a union of groups or nations

definitions.text: quite a long way to go
definitions.meaning: an old unit of distance of about three miles

explanation.definitionFit: A union of states is so called; it was also an old distance measure of about three miles.

clue.text: What circular letter said for artist

indicators.note: the words are spoken aloud to give the name

parts.note: what followed by O, the round letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a circular letter said about a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular letter' sounds like a mailshot, but it is O, the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Watteau was a French Rococo painter.

clue.text: Flower for excessively sentimental daughter

parts.note: twee means sweet or cute to a sickly degree

explanation.surface: A bloom given to a cloyingly sweet girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a flowing thing, a river: the Tweed runs between Scotland and England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish river is a flower in the crossword sense of something that flows.

clue.text: Rough form of sound

parts.note: a rough sketch of shape, read playfully as the form of the word for sound, which can mean bay or channel

explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a sketch giving only the main shape, a rough form.

clue.text: Without queen, this bid wouldn't be on

parts.note: off means not on, as a cancelled event
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A card player says that without the queen this bid would not stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: without ER (queen) the word would be OFF, not on.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer is a bid, as at an auction.

clue.text: The title is announced of season for ballet

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for title is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a title is a right or legal claim
taken as written
spring is a season of the year

explanation.surface: The name of a season is made public for a dance piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Stravinsky's 1913 ballet caused a riot at its Paris premiere.

clue.text: Like the meaning of Basingstoke, said Gilbert

definitions.text: Like the meaning of Basingstoke, said Gilbert

parts.words: Like the meaning of Basingstoke, said Gilbert
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's Ruddigore, the town name Basingstoke is a secret code word used to calm Mad Margaret

explanation.definitionFit: In the operetta, the word works as a concealed signal whose sense is secret.

clue.text: Faking coins without really expert touch, initially

indicators.note: here without means outside: the coins surround the other letters

parts.note: pence are British coins

indicators.note: the opening letters of really, expert and touch are taken

explanation.surface: Counterfeiting money without a genuinely skilled hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Faking is pretending, a false show.
